formulations.label: Gel 2% (mucosal / urethral)
formulations.note: The UK SmPC used is for a sterile single-ingredient lidocaine hydrochloride 2% gel in pre-filled syringes (urethral and rectal use). No other single-ingredient lidocaine 2% gel SmPC was found in the UK.

src.q: 1 ml gel contains 20.1 mg lidocaine hydrochloride
Clear, nearly colourless, sterile gel.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Surface anaesthesia and lubrication of the male and female urethra (cystoscopy, catheterisation, sounding and other endourethral procedures), for proctoscopy and rectoscopy, and for symptomatic treatment of pain with cystitis. Licensed in adults, adolescents and children from 2 years.

src.q: The male and female urethra during cystoscopy, catheterisation, exploration by sound and other endourethral operations; Proctoscopy and rectoscopy; Symptomatic treatment of pain in connection with cystitis.
is indicated in adults, adolescents and children from 2 years of age.

items.t: The dose must be individually adjusted by an experienced physician; use the lowest dose that gives effective anaesthesia.

src.q: The dose must be individually adjusted by an experienced physician.
The lowest dosage that results in effective anaesthesia should be used to avoid high plasma levels and serious undesirable effects.

items.t: When used with other lidocaine-containing products, count the total lidocaine dose from all of them.

src.q: the total dose contributed by all formulations must be taken into consideration

items.t: Usually 20 ml gel (about 400 mg lidocaine hydrochloride): instil about 10 ml slowly, apply a penile clamp for at least 5 minutes, then instil the rest. For sounding or cystoscopy 10-20 ml; may be repeated once with 10-20 ml. Do not exceed about 800 mg lidocaine hydrochloride. For catheterisation of the anterior urethra 5-10 ml is usually enough.

src.q: For adequate analgesia in males, 20 ml gel (approximately 400 mg lidocaine hydrochloride) is usually required.
A penile clamp is then applied for at least 5 minutes at the corona, after which the rest of the gel is instilled.
The maximum dose of approximately 800 mg lidocaine hydrochloride must not be exceeded.
small volumes (5-10 ml, i.e. approximately 100-200mg lidocaine hydrochloride) are usually adequate for lubrication

items.t: Usually 5-10 ml gel (about 100-200 mg lidocaine hydrochloride) instilled in small portions; allow at least 5 minutes before the procedure.

src.q: Usually, 5-10 ml of gel (approximately 100-200 mg lidocaine hydrochloride) are instilled in small portions to fill the whole urethra.
at least 5 minutes should be allowed prior to performing urological procedures

items.t: Usually 10-20 ml gel once a day for one week at first; then frequency and duration are set by the physician. Maximum 20 ml (about 400 mg lidocaine hydrochloride) once a day.

src.q: At the beginning of the treatment, the gel is usually administered once a day for one week.
The maximum dose is: 20 ml (approximately 400 mg lidocaine hydrochloride) once a day.

items.t: Instil 10-20 ml gel and lubricate the endoscope. If combined with other lidocaine products, total lidocaine hydrochloride should not exceed 378 mg; absorption from the rectum is particularly high.

src.q: Instillation of 10 - 20 ml (approximately 200 - 400mg lidocaine hydrochloride) gel is recommended for adequate analgesia
When combined with other lidocaine products, the total dose of lidocaine hydrochloride should not exceed 378 mg.
The degree of absorption is particularly high in the rectum.

items.t: Maximum recommended daily dose in adults: about 800 mg lidocaine hydrochloride (40 ml gel in the urethra and bladder).

src.q: The maximum recommended daily dose for adults is approximately 800 mg lidocaine hydrochloride.

items.t: Elderly, debilitated, acutely ill or septic patients: give reduced doses; do not exceed 2.9 mg/kg lidocaine hydrochloride.

src.q: Debilitated, elderly, acutely ill patients and patients with sepsis should be given reduced doses
The maximum dose of 2.9 mg/kg lidocaine hydrochloride should not be exceeded in these special populations.

items.t: Contraindicated in children under 2 years.

src.q: Glydo 20 mg/ml gel is contraindicated in children < 2 years of age

items.t: Children 2-12 years and adolescents: effect not well demonstrated, so the physician must assess use; no specific dose. Absorption may be higher in children, so use caution. Children 2-12 years: do not exceed 2.9 mg/kg lidocaine hydrochloride.

src.q: the effect of lidocaine hydrochloride gels is not well demonstrated and therefore, its use should be assessed by the physician
The systemic absorption of lidocaine can be increased in children and caution is accordingly required.
In general, the maximum dose of 2.9 mg/kg lidocaine hydrochloride should not be exceeded in children aged 2 to 12 years

items.t: Hypersensitivity to lidocaine or any excipient; hypersensitivity to amide-type local anaesthetics; children under 2 years.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1. Hypersensitivity to local anaesthetics of the amide type. Children under 2 years.

items.t: Too much gel or short dose intervals can cause high plasma levels and serious effects (CNS and cardiovascular toxicity). Absorption is high from wounds and mucosa: use with caution with damaged mucosa or sepsis at the site, an inflamed or ulcerated urethra, or if gel enters the bladder; risk is higher in children and the elderly.

src.q: Excessive dosage, or short intervals between doses, can result in high plasma levels and serious undesirable effects.
should be used with caution in patients with traumatised mucosa and/or sepsis in the region of the proposed application
consequently to overdose with central nervous and cardiovascular undesirable effects (see also section 4.9), especially in children and elderly patients

items.t: Take special care (risk of high blood levels) in elderly or frail patients, sepsis, epilepsy, bradycardia or impaired cardiovascular function, heart failure, AV block, shock, renal or hepatic impairment, respiratory dysfunction, and myasthenia gravis.

src.q: some patients require special attention to prevent potentially dangerous side effects
Patients with bradycardia or impaired cardiovascular function
Patients with heart failure or with AV block. - Patients with shock. - Patients with impaired renal function and hepatic disease
Patients suffering from myasthenia gravis; these are particularly sensitive to local anaesthetics.

items.t: Methaemoglobinaemia has been reported with local anaesthetics. G6PD deficiency and hereditary or idiopathic methaemoglobinaemia increase susceptibility; in G6PD deficiency methylene blue is ineffective and cannot be given.

src.q: Cases of methaemoglobinaemia have been reported in association with local anaesthetic use.
Patients with defective glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase, hereditary or idiopathic methaemoglobinemia are more susceptible
methylene blue therapy cannot be given

items.t: Acute porphyria: possibly porphyrinogenic; use only on strong or urgent indications with close monitoring.

src.q: Lidocaine is possibly porphyrinogenic and should only be used in patients with acute porphyria on strong or urgent indications, while being closely monitored.

items.t: Patients on class III anti-arrhythmics (for example amiodarone): close surveillance and consider ECG monitoring (additive cardiac effects).

src.q: should be under close surveillance and ECG monitoring considered, since cardiac effects may be additive

items.t: Other lidocaine products or other amide-type local anaesthetics (or related agents): should not be used together, as toxic effects are additive. Class I anti-arrhythmics (such as mexiletine): use with caution.

src.q: should not be used in patients receiving lidocaine or other local anaesthetics or agents structurally related to amide-type local anaesthetics since the toxic effects are additive
Class I antiarrhythmic drugs (such as mexiletine) should be used with caution

items.t: Beta-blockers (for example propranolol, metoprolol) and calcium channel antagonists (for example diltiazem, verapamil): use lidocaine with caution (possible additive cardiac effects). Beta-blockers also reduce lidocaine clearance; allow for accumulation.

src.q: lidocaine must be used with caution in patients receiving other anti-arrhythmics such as beta-blockers (e.g. propranolol, metoprolol) or calcium channel antagonists (e.g. diltiazem, verapamil)
Due account should therefore be taken of the possibility of accumulation of lidocaine.

items.t: Methaemoglobin-inducing medicines (for example sulphonamides, nitrofurantoin, phenytoin, phenobarbital) may make methaemoglobinaemia worse.

src.q: Methaemoglobinaemia may be accentuated in patients already taking methaemoglobin-inducing medicinal products (e.g. sulphonamides, nitrofurantoin, phenytoin, phenobarbital).

items.t: CYP3A4 and/or CYP1A2 inhibitors (for example erythromycin, fluvoxamine, amiodarone, cimetidine, ritonavir) can raise lidocaine levels, but at recommended gel doses the systemic exposure is low and these interactions are not expected to be clinically significant.

src.q: Concurrent administration of lidocaine with inhibitors of CYP 3A4 and/or CYP 1A2 may lead to accelerated plasma concentrations of lidocaine.
the systemic exposure is low and therefore the above- mentioned metabolic interactions are not expected to be of clinical significance

items.t: Renal impairment: lidocaine doses must be reduced (to prevent metabolite accumulation). No threshold or measure is given.

src.q: lidocaine doses must be reduced in patients with renal or hepatic impairment to prevent potential metabolite accumulation

items.t: Hepatic impairment: lidocaine doses must be reduced; half-life may be prolonged two-fold or more with liver dysfunction. No severity grading is given.

src.q: lidocaine doses must be reduced in patients with renal or hepatic impairment
The half-life may be prolonged two-fold or more in patients with liver dysfunction.

items.t: Limited human data; lidocaine crosses the placenta. Animal studies at topical-relevant exposure show no harm. May be considered in pregnancy if clinically needed.

src.q: There are limited amount of data from the use of lidocaine in pregnant women. Lidocaine crosses the placenta.
may be considered during pregnancy, if clinically needed

items.t: Lidocaine passes into breast milk, but at therapeutic doses of the gel no effects on the breastfed infant are anticipated.

src.q: Lidocaine is excreted in human milk, but at therapeutic doses of Glydo 20 mg/ml gel no effects on breastfed newborns/infants are anticipated.

items.t: No human fertility data; no impairment of fertility in rat studies.

src.q: There are no data on the effect of lidocaine on fertility in human.

items.t: No common or very common effects listed. Rare: hypersensitivity, anaphylactic reaction, contact dermatitis. Very rare: application site irritation. Undesirable effects are unlikely if used as recommended.

src.q: Undesirable effects are unlikely to occur after the use of Glydo 20 mg/ml gel, as long as the medicinal product is used as recommended
Hypersensitivity, Immune system anaphylactic reaction, contact disorders dermatitis General administration site irritation

items.t: Systemic toxicity from high blood levels: early signs are yawning, restlessness, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, slurred speech, ataxia, hearing and vision disturbance; then twitching, convulsions, loss of consciousness, respiratory depression, coma, hypotension, heart block and cardiac arrest. Stop administration at once; treat seizures and support the airway; start CPR if circulation stops.

src.q: yawning, restlessness, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, dysarthria, ataxia, hearing and vision disorders
hypotension and cardiovascular collapse can be expected, followed by complete heart block and cardiac arrest
If signs of acute toxicity occur during administration of the local anaesthetic, administration of the anaesthetic should be stopped immediately.

items.t: Urethral use: clean and disinfect the urethral opening, instil the gel slowly and evenly, and wait for full effect (5-15 minutes). Anaesthesia lasts about 20-30 minutes.

src.q: Clean and disinfect the external orifice of the urethra.
The gel should be instilled slowly and evenly into the urethra.
Duration of anaesthesia is approximately 20 to 30 minutes.

items.t: Keep strictly to the dose and instructions given; report any symptoms of toxicity (for example dizziness, nausea, vomiting, slurred speech, unsteadiness, hearing or vision disturbance).
